extracted.intended_audience: general public, stakeholders, and other federal agencies invited to comment on USCIS information collection notices and related Federal Register actions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting public comments on U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) information-collection and related Federal Register notices under the Paperwork Reduction Act, and understanding related procedural actions (extensions, reinstatements, TPS terminations, approvals).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA public comment topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain comments regarding the nature of the information collection, the categories of respondents, the estimated burden (i.e., the time, effort, and resources used by the respondents to respond), the estimated cost to the respondent, and the actual information collection instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notices (published in the Federal Register) invite the general public and other Federal agencies to comment on the proposed revision/extension/reinstatement of information collections; comments should address the listed topics (nature, respondent categories, burden, cost, instruments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of information-collection actions and how they are characterized
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS actions are described as 'Extension, Without Change, of a Currently Approved Collection'; 'Revision of a Currently Approved Collection'; 'Reinstatement, With Change, of a Previously Approved Collection for Which Approval Has Expired'; and similar formulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice type signals the procedural posture and what is being requested (e.g., extension without change means continuing existing approval; reinstatement with change indicates resubmitting an expired collection with modifications). Notices typically state the agency will submit or has submitted the collection request to OMB for review and clearance in accordance with the PRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of issuance to allow additional public comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this notice is to allow an additional 30 days for public comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some notices explicitly state they are being published to provide an extra opportunity for public comment (commonly used in reinstatement/OMB-review contexts). Commenters should note and meet any specified additional timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information-collection notices must include burden and cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices must present the estimated burden (time, effort, resources) on respondents and the estimated cost to respondents, and make the information collection instruments available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters can and should evaluate (and comment on) the reasonableness and accuracy of the burden and cost estimates and review the actual instruments provided (e.g., forms, questionnaires) when available (PDFs linked in the notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary Protected Status (TPS) termination decision standard
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing country conditions and consulting with appropriate U.S. Government agencies, the Secretary determined that [country] no longer continues to meet the conditions for designation for Temporary Protected Status; therefore, the Secretary is terminating the TPS designation as required by statute (with an effective date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice describes the decision-making process (review of country conditions and interagency consultation) and states the statutory effect and effective date; it also explains the practical consequence that nationals of the country will no longer have TPS after the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of approval for credentialing organizations (informational notification)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS issues a notice to inform the public of the approval of a new credentialing organization for specified immigration-related purposes (for example, credentialing of certain health care workers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notices serve to inform stakeholders of approvals that affect credential recognition for immigration purposes; they are informational but relevant to affected parties (employers, applicants, credentialing bodies).
